rows.INVALID: key collision above 32 qubits -- see CORRECTION_2026-09-04

CORRECTION_2026-09-04.what: The L=6 row is invalid and must not be quoted. Rows L=3,4,5 stand.
CORRECTION_2026-09-04.why: 6x6 is 36 qubits and this run used the numba engine, whose key is x | (z << 32) -- lossless only to 32 qubits. Above that, x needs bit 32, where z's bit 0 lands: Z_0 and X_32 pack to the same uint64, and the engine writes d[key] = value, so one term overwrites the other.
CORRECTION_2026-09-04.is_it_actually_triggered: Yes, measured. The same 6x6 propagation was re-run with the string engine (no packing, no collision) at looser truncation: at delta=1e-3 the support already reaches qubit 33 with 42 terms past index 31, and at delta=1e-4, 1214 terms. A looser delta keeps strictly fewer terms, so production delta=1e-8 reached it too.
CORRECTION_2026-09-04.direction_of_the_error: Undercount. Colliding terms share one dict slot, so centre_terms at L=6 is lower than the truth and the coefficients of the survivors are wrong.
CORRECTION_2026-09-04.what_this_costs: The saturation conclusion rested on this row alone: ratio_vs_prev 48.33 (3->4), 5.13 (4->5), 0.988 (5->6). Only the 0.988 says 'saturated', and it is the corrupt one -- and an undercount biases the ratio downward, i.e. toward the conclusion that was drawn. What survives is deceleration (48.3 -> 5.13), which is consistent with approaching saturation but does not demonstrate it. T2's cost estimate must not lean on it.
CORRECTION_2026-09-04.how_to_recover_it: Widen the packed key to two uint64 per mask, or re-run 6x6 with the string engine (no size limit, but ~7x slower than numba on a 2.5 h run, and 14M string-keyed terms is several GB). scripts/03h_lightcone_production_delta.py now refuses n>32 rather than producing another bad row.
